answer: Here is one mechanism that works: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because ferrous only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, garden is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any anchor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
